stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to transformers, Llama architecture, and the AI community.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: OpenAI’s next big AI model has ‘entered the AGI era’
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: OpenAI has announced its next major model, GPT-6 Astra, claiming it represents a 'generational leap in capability'.
The new model is touted for significant advancements across multiple domains, including cybersecurity, software engineering, and scientific research.
GPT-6 Astra is the first model to meet OpenAI's internal 'critical cybersecurity capability threshold'.

stories.title: Nvidia buys Hugging Face, the GitHub of AI, for $13 billion
stories.author: Michael Acton, Financial Times
bullet_points: Nvidia has acquired Hugging Face, a major platform described as the 'GitHub of AI'.
The acquisition is valued at $13 billion, signaling a massive strategic move in the AI ecosystem.
Nvidia has committed to keeping Hugging Face open-source despite taking control of the platform.

stories.title: GPT-6 Astra
stories.author: kibae
bullet_points: The news references 'GPT-6 Astra,' suggesting a potential next-generation or advanced iteration of OpenAI's GPT models.
The link points to an OpenAI deployment safety page, indicating a formal or internal release/testing environment for this model.
This represents significant industry news regarding the ongoing development and scaling of frontier Large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes key ML components such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks, including context gathering and tool calling, running locally.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed improvement according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Congressman says TikTok backed out of a meeting to avoid child safety questions
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: TikTok reportedly withdrew from a congressional roundtable to preemptively avoid scrutiny over its child safety practices.
The withdrawal comes after negotiations were underway to have TikTok's Chief Security Officer testify before the House Select Committee on China.
The incident highlights ongoing political and regulatory tensions surrounding the platform's data security and ties to the Chinese government.

stories.title: Microsoft opens up Xbox Cloud Gaming with new pay-as-you-go option
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is introducing a pay-as-you-go option for Xbox Cloud Gaming.
This new model allows users to access the service without a full Xbox Game Pass subscription.
The change is set to roll out in November and targets infrequent cloud gaming users.

stories.title: Four major AI models suffer rare overlapping downtime
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Four leading AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini) experienced simultaneous service disruptions.
The event highlights potential systemic vulnerabilities or shared infrastructure issues across major AI providers.
The overlapping nature of the downtime is notable, suggesting a rare, widespread technical incident.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research focuses on enhancing LLM performance in highly challenging coding competitions (e.g., IOI, ICPC).
A specialized pipeline combining problem curation, synthetic reasoning traces, SFT, and RL was developed for model training.
The study compares fine-tuned models (Nemotron-3-Nano-CC and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC) to test the efficacy of different training methodologies.

stories.title: The Implications of Linguistic Illegibility for LLM Security
stories.author: James Mickens
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of 'linguistic illegibility' in LLMs.
Argues that external language outputs and mechanistic probes are unreliable for understanding internal LLM computation.
Highlights a fundamental challenge in LLM interpretability and security.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research introduces a specialized pipeline (SFT + RL) to enhance LLM performance in competitive programming.
Two models, Nemotron-3-Nano-CC and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC, were trained using 22,000 curated problems to test reasoning capabilities.
The work addresses the challenge of evaluating LLM reasoning in highly rigorous settings like IOI and ICPC.

stories.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
stories.author: Zheng Liu
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between general AI agents and practical, domain-specific ML execution.
It proposes 'Repo-To-Skill' to distill operational knowledge embedded in GitHub repositories into usable AI skills.
This aims to bridge the gap where agents know a method but lack the practical 'know-how' to implement it successfully.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary AI platforms and local, open-source LLMs.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Microsoft slashes Xbox Cloud Gaming to just 15 hours a month for Ultimate subscribers
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is significantly reducing the cloud gaming allowance for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers.
The service, previously offering unlimited cloud gaming across all tiers, will now cap usage at 15 hours per month.
This change marks a shift in the service model less than a year after its initial rollout.

stories.title: Just like a fruit fly, a new algorithm never forgets old scents
stories.author: Federica Sgorbissa
bullet_points: A new algorithm inspired by insect learning is being introduced.
The technique utilizes 'sparse coding' to enable fast learning in AI models.
A key feature of this method is its ability to avoid 'catastrophic forgetting' of old information.

stories.title: I rented a car, and within hours, my driver's license was for sale
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A massive, real-time data breach is reportedly under investigation by the FBI.
The breach is linked to the personal data of individuals, exemplified by a driver's license being put up for sale.
The story highlights the severe risks associated with personal data security in modern digital systems.

stories.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
stories.author: Roei Herzig
bullet_points: Current web agents utilize world models for action selection by predicting future web states.
These models are often trained using supervised next-state prediction, yielding fixed representations (e.g., HTML snapshots).
The training objective is noted as being misaligned with the downstream ranker, which requires discriminative state predictions.

stories.title: Towards Trustworthy Autonomous Robots: An Explainable AI-Based Decision Framework
stories.author: Cagri Temel
bullet_points: Addresses the critical auditability challenge in deep learning-powered autonomous robots.
Introduces TRACE (Transparent Reasoning Architecture for Credible Execution) to ensure decision traceability.
The framework structures decision-making across four auditable layers, linking actions back to sensor evidence.

stories.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
stories.author: Zhang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of performing Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in complex 5G/6G telecom networks.
It identifies that standard Large Language Models (LLMs) suffer from hallucination and poor alignment when applied directly to structured network evidence.
The research proposes a structured reasoning framework to leverage LLMs for evidence-grounded diagnosis in telecom operations.

stories.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
stories.author: Suproteem Sarkar
bullet_points: The research investigates the coherence of probabilistic forecasts generated by large language models (LLMs).
It addresses the growing trend of users relying on LLMs for complex life decisions and predictions.
The evaluation method builds upon de Finetti's theorem to test the underlying world model consistency of the models.

stories.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
stories.author: Dongrui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SafeEvolve, a novel method for safety alignment in LLM-based agents.
Addresses the dual safety risks arising from both LLM responses and multi-step execution trajectories.
Proposes a co-evolutionary approach that jointly shapes the base model and the interaction harness using agent experience.

stories.title: Measurement-Driven Sub-Network Selection for On-Premise Retrieval-Augmented Factory Agents
stories.author: Athanasios Bachoumis
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of deploying large AI models (like RAG agents) on resource-constrained, on-premise factory hardware.
Proposes a novel approach where model selection is treated as a post-adaptation problem, moving beyond simple parameter count as a quality metric.
Demonstrates that general model capability degrades predictably with size, but the quality of retrieval-augmented answers is less sensitive to parameter count.

stories.title: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces
stories.author: Oiwi Parker Jones
bullet_points: The paper addresses the lack of a standardized metric for evaluating Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs).
Speech BCIs are a critical technology for restoring speech in individuals with paralysis and advancing human-computer interaction.
Current research comparability is hindered by variations in datasets, recording methods, and vocabulary used across different systems.

stories.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
stories.author: Roei Herzig
bullet_points: Current web agents utilize world models for action selection by predicting future web states.
These models are typically trained using supervised next-state prediction, generating fixed representations.
The training objective is noted as being misaligned with the downstream ranker, which requires discriminative state predictions.

stories.title: Graph Machine: Towards Better Pretraining via Edges
stories.author: Lintai Hou
bullet_points: Introduces Graph Machine (GM), a novel architecture for improved pretraining.
GM maintains an $O(n)$-sized state accessible via sparse, dynamic routing, overcoming limitations of fixed-size or static routing methods.
The architecture utilizes differentiable, pointer-like 'edges' for state access, replacing a significant portion of dense Transformer layers.

stories.title: GRADSOLVE: fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles on GPUs
stories.author: Alessio Spurio Mancini
bullet_points: Addresses a critical bottleneck in scientific computing: the trade-off between fast ODE ensemble solving on GPUs and the ability to compute exact reverse-mode gradients.
Introduces 'GRADSOLVE,' a new method designed to provide fast, exact gradients for ODE ensembles specifically optimized for GPU acceleration.
The research targets applications where derivatives of ODE solutions with respect to parameters are necessary, such as in advanced simulations and machine learning models.

stories.title: UE5M3 FP4 Block Scaling for Stable Language Model Pretraining
stories.author: Paul Balanca
bullet_points: The paper addresses the instability of 4-bit floating-point (FP4) pretraining in large language models (LLMs).
The proposed solution replaces standard E2M1 payloads with unsigned E5M3 block scales to achieve a wider dynamic range.
This new scaling method allows for periodic tensor scaling, improving stability compared to existing techniques like NVIDIA's Transformer Engine recipe.

stories.title: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
stories.author: Omri Abend
bullet_points: The paper proposes that naturally occurring user feedback is a highly actionable learning signal for LLMs.
It challenges the prevailing view that user feedback is inherently too noisy or difficult to leverage.
The authors suggest that the perceived ineffectiveness of user feedback is due to systematic biases in current evaluation methods.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research focuses on enhancing Large Language Models (LLMs) for competitive programming, a rigorous test of reasoning.
A specialized pipeline combining problem curation, synthetic reasoning traces, SFT, and RL was developed for model training.
The study compares performance using two models, Nemotron-3-Nano-CC (SFT+RL) and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC (SFT only).

stories.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
stories.author: Suproteem Sarkar
bullet_points: The research investigates the coherence of probabilistic forecasts generated by language models.
It addresses the growing user reliance on LLMs for high-stakes life decisions (e.g., economic, disaster risk).
The evaluation methodology builds upon a theorem by de Finetti to test model consistency.

stories.title: DiscoSign: Discourse-Aware Text to Sign Language Gloss Translation
stories.author: Colin Lea
bullet_points: Introduces DiscoSign, a new computational approach for text-to-sign language gloss translation.
Addresses limitations of traditional sentence-level processing by incorporating discourse-aware features.
Utilizes a modular Large Language Model (LLM) framework to handle phenomena like spatial coreference resolution.

stories.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
stories.author: Xiaodong Gu
bullet_points: The research addresses the high computational cost associated with evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) agents.
It introduces 'early outcome prediction' as a method to reduce evaluation expenses, complementing existing benchmark distillation techniques.
This work aims to make the iterative development and refinement of LLM agents more economically feasible.

stories.title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding
stories.author: Jun Yu
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of using Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for continuous video stream processing.
Proposes 'ShallowStream,' a method designed to index shallowly before performing deep analysis for efficient streaming video understanding.
Highlights the broad real-world applicability of efficient video understanding, including autonomous driving and industrial monitoring.

stories.title: HyperStyler: Low-resource Authorship Style Transfer via Context-aware Style Navigation and Hypernetworks
stories.author: Chiehyeon Lim
bullet_points: Introduces HyperStyler, a new method for Low-resource Authorship Style Transfer (LAST).
Addresses limitations in existing methods where static author embeddings average out context-dependent stylistic variation.
Utilizes Context-aware Style Navigation and Hypernetworks to improve style fidelity while preserving semantic meaning with few examples.

stories.title: Untangling the Mechanisms of Misleading Context in Medical Question Answering
stories.author: Noémie Elhadad
bullet_points: Investigates how misleading context can corrupt the expert-level medical judgment of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The research examines the model's susceptibility, disclosure, reasoning mechanisms, and monitorability when presented with flawed medical context.
Uses the MedMisBench dataset to analyze these vulnerabilities in medical question answering systems.

stories.title: Qwen 3.8 27B available on Cerebras at 1500 tokens/s
stories.author: altertable
bullet_points: Qwen 3.8 27B model is now accessible on Cerebras hardware.
The model demonstrates a high inference speed of 1500 tokens/s on the specified platform.
This highlights the performance capabilities of large language models when run on specialized AI accelerators.

stories.title: Porting my 1993 Amiga game to Godot, with an LLM reading the 68000 assembly
stories.author: rabahs
bullet_points: A developer ported a 1993 Amiga game written in MC68000 assembly to the Godot engine.
The porting process heavily involved using an LLM (Claude Fable 5) to assist with the assembly code analysis.
The project highlights the emerging use of LLMs not just for content generation, but for complex, low-level code translation and understanding legacy systems.
